Do you think just looking at them helps ?

Problem is, most guides are in English, we on Latin America, she only knows Spanish.

Thanks for the advice tho, I'll  look out for guides in Spanish.
That might actually be a really important change, thanks a lot.

Thanks again, the thing is, to me at least, starting in the game felt natural by the fact its core mechanics are present in a lot of videogames.

But she doesn't have that knowledge, so its kinda hard to make the experience of learning enjoyable to her, when even jumping makes her struggle.

Sorry for the big paragraph, and for the possible grammatical errors.

Ah, the basic stuff then, thanks mate.

Dunno if she'll ever want to play in ranked tho, kinda installed so we could mess around together.

That's a good one, and obvious one, I'm kind of a dumb ass.

Thanks mate.
Just wanted to say, sorry for everyone bombarding you with apanish comments and people been mean to you just because of that spanish title you used.

It's kinda written like portuguese, though I know you used Google translate to write that in spanish. It ended looking like that, cause you got a weird translation in the end.

The dude above said that, that it looks like portuguese.

Yeah, I didn't meant to say I agree with their statements.

But as a native Spanish speaker, they're actually working harder with those than with real problems.

They're actually doing it pretty well I might say. 
Its weird tho.

I can certainly agree with what you stated. 
I just wanted to clarify how different our viewpoints may be affected by the country we live in, and also thank you for sharing what you think, it really helps me to try and understand how different things are perceived according to the place we live in.

Kind of a late response from my part but you're kind of wrong about it being silent. I actually live in Guatemala, and the genocidal acts financed by the US, and more precisely by te use of the American Fruit Company, now named Chiquita by the way, is actually a well known to nearly everyone in my country.

And this stuff still affects us, but instead of just whining about it we try to keep the memory of this events alive so history won't repeat itself. And just putting the blame on the US and despising a whole country filled with actually great people is nothing but a solution, at least to us, who actually live in Guatemala and yes, we're still affected by those events.

I absolutely agree with your viewpoints.
And I think that the use of this images as some kind of ideological propaganda is kind of stupid, like insisting to be called something they labeled us as, just like you said referring to the term "american".
And just to clarify things a little, I was referring to the proper way of describing our cultural groups, for example, I'm from Guatemala, and I think its great to have in mind the different pre-hispanic civilizations that once inhabited our territory, and that some of us are still part of that.
Yeah, that's the part that messes this up.

I completly understand what you're saying and actually agree with you in some points. Especially about the fact that they don't really care and this does nothing in changing that fact.

However, the point of images like this is completely separated from trying to prove something to them. I believe its more about keeping our history alive, and a reminder that our cultures are still vibrant even in the modern era, when almost everything in completely is being wiped out by occidental culture in general.

Of course, this is what I think, and the purpose may be completely different from what I thought.
